standard.title: Questioning and Predicting
standard.description: pose questions to explore observed simple patterns and relationships and make predictions based on experiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can ask questions about the world around them (F band). They now begin to pose questions about patterns and relationships specifically, and make predictions grounded in their experiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students pose simple investigable questions about observed patterns and relationships, and make experience-based predictions before observing or investigating.

nodes.label: Questions explore patterns and relationships
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can pose a question about a simple pattern or relationship in an observed phenomenon, distinguishing it from a question about naming or describing.
nodes.minimum_width: Students pose at least one question about a pattern or relationship for a given observation context.
nodes.typical_width: Students pose questions about patterns (seasonal plant changes, weather patterns) and relationships (push strength and distance, plant care and growth) across Y1 science contexts, and explain what their question is trying to find out.
wider: Pose questions about how animals meet their needs in particular places — exploring habitat-need relationships
Pose questions about push and pull relationships: 'Does a toy car go further if it is pushed harder?' — examining force-motion relationships
Make predictions about types of animals and plants they might observe in a particular place — connecting habitat knowledge to prediction
nodes.hinge_reason: N2's prediction-before-investigation sequence requires students to have a question to predict about. Without posing an investigable question, there is no anchor for making and checking an experience-based prediction.
success_criteria: Poses a question about a pattern or relationship (not just a naming question) for a given observation
Explains what the question is trying to find out

nodes.label: Predictions are based on prior experiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make a prediction before an observation or investigation and explain what experience the prediction is based on.
nodes.minimum_width: Students make one prediction and explain what experience it is based on.
nodes.typical_width: Students make predictions across Y1 science contexts (plant needs, force effects, seasonal changes) and explain the experience that grounds each prediction — distinguishing a prediction from a guess.
wider: Make predictions about patterns of observable phenomena such as seasonal plant changes or temperature patterns across seasons
Make predictions about plant needs: 'I think a plant will die if it does not get enough water' — grounding prediction in care experience
Consult with First Nations Australians to compare observations of animal tracks and evaluate identifications (AC9S1I05)
success_criteria: Makes a prediction before an observation or investigation
Explains what experience the prediction is based on
